scope: Proposition 4.7 (Coupling by independent marked squares) of the manuscript “SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions” (preprints/SLE3-universality-for-weak-finite-range-Ising-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 44a7837e35328259), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 40. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let the physical torus law µλ,N be at the temperature of Theorem 4.5, with trajectory bound (4.24). Let KN = max{k ≥ 0 : Lsk ≤ N/10} for all sufficiently large N. There is a coupling of σ(0) ∼ µ0,N , σ(λ) ∼ µλ,N , and Bernoulli marks Mk,x, 0 ≤ k ≤ KN , x ∈ TN , with the following properties. The marks are mutually independent and independent of σ(0), and P(Mk,x = 1) ≤ Cϵ2−k s−2 k . (4.31) Except on an event of probability o(1) as N → ∞, σ(λ) can be obtained from σ(0) by changing spins only inside the union of the marked squares BLsk (x). The values of the changed spins may depend on all previous refreshes. The constant and the exceptional probability are independent of test domains and exterior configurations. Enlarging these squares by any fixed number of lattice steps preserves the conclusion.
